# OpenDDIL Customer Overlay — Worked Example — LLM Context

This repository (`openddil-customer-bundle-example`) is a publishable
worked example of the OpenDDIL customer-overlay pattern. It demonstrates
how customer-specific feeds, ICDs, and ontology entries layer on top of
the OSS demo without contaminating the OSS code.

## Purpose

The OSS OpenDDIL demo (`openddil-demo`) runs DIS-only out of the box.
Real customers have proprietary ICDs and feeds (HTTP sensors, AMQP
simulators, custom protocols). This example shows the overlay pattern:

- A separate `docker-compose.customer.yml` adds customer-specific
  services on top of the OSS base.
- Customer Bronze→Silver mappings live in `dynamic-mappings/`.
- Customer ontology aliases (asset_identity, platform_variant) layer
  over the OSS ontology base.
- Customer egress vocabularies (e.g., OK/DEGRADED/CRITICAL or
  FMC/PMC/NMC) live in `dynamic-mappings/egress/`.

All content here is **placeholder** — invented feed shapes, hull IDs,
and vendor names. Real customers fork this template to a PRIVATE
bundle outside the `openddil/` workspace.

## Key Files

- `docker-compose.customer.yml` — adds `rabbitmq`, `sim-a` AMQP
  publisher, `redpanda-connect-sim-a-amqp` (AMQP→Kafka), and the
  System B egress Connect container.
- `connect/openddil-customer-connect.yaml` — sim-a Bronze→Silver
  Connect pipeline.
- `connect/connect-egress.yaml` — Kafka→AMQP egress for System B.
- `dynamic-mappings/sim-a-mapping.yaml` — placeholder sim-a Bloblang.
- `dynamic-mappings/egress/system-b-egress.yaml` — default egress
  envelope (OK/DEGRADED/CRITICAL vocab).
- `dynamic-mappings/egress/system-b-egress-fmc.yaml` — alt egress
  vocabulary (FMC/PMC/NMC) for the same envelope.
- `ontology/asset_identity_aliases.yaml`,
  `ontology/platform_variant_aliases.yaml` — placeholder dis+sim_a
  aliases. Layer over the OSS base via bind-mount in the Connect
  containers.
- `tests/_example_helpers.py` — re-exports OSS generic helpers
  (`_cm_helpers`) AND provides sim-a/egress test plumbing. Private
  bundles cross-import this to inherit one import root.
- `tests/integration/run_all.py` — composed-stack regression gate
  (OSS base + this overlay; 4 cross-boundary tests).

## Composition Modes

This overlay is designed to layer cleanly:

| Mode | `docker compose -f ...` |
|------|--------------------------|
| OSS only | `openddil-demo/docker-compose.yml` |
| OSS + example | OSS + `openddil/openddil-customer-bundle-example/docker-compose.customer.yml` |
| OSS + private | OSS + `<customer-private>/docker-compose.customer.yml` |
| OSS + example + private | All three |

Compose path resolution: relative paths in ALL `-f` files resolve
relative to the FIRST `-f` file's directory (always
`openddil-demo`). This file uses `../openddil-customer-bundle-example/...`
to find its own assets when invoked from inside `openddil-demo`.

## Rules

- This example is publishable; real customer bundles are NOT and live
  outside `openddil/`.
- The cross-import contract from `_example_helpers.py` is consumed by
  private bundles — renaming a public helper here breaks them.
- The overlay only references registry images; no `build:` directives.

## Docker Compose

Overlays the OSS base. The OSS base references
`image: ghcr.io/edgy-solutions/openddil/...:latest` for OpenDDIL
services. Connect containers in this overlay use
`docker.redpanda.com/redpandadata/connect:latest`.

NEVER add a `build:` to `docker-compose.customer.yml`. Source mounts
for dev hot-reload of OSS services live in
`openddil-demo/docker-compose.override.yml`, not here.
